# Preserve native Build working context

Slug: build-continuity
Model: .kogen/intents/build-continuity/model.qnt invariants=Safety seed=21 samples=100 steps=40
Acceptance:
- .kogen/intents/build-continuity/acceptance.feature
- features/steps/build_continuity_steps.js

Deliver one native core change for bounded working windows and faithful private source provenance. Replace append-only Build/reviewer replay with explicit LOCAL working-window resets at completed safe boundaries. Keep the existing provider, model/effort, stateless Responses transport, independent review, verification and exact approval. No new provider capability is required. This is not a total-Build token limit or a guarantee of model convergence.

## Decisions
- Bound the rendered next request, preserve full ordered history privately, and stop honestly when irreducible material cannot fit. Never truncate authority or orphan tools. (source: request)
- Retain successful original request/Q&A and source identity independently of the shaper's transcription; surface diagnostic comparison at the existing approval boundary and provide retrieval during Build and fresh independent review. Original requests and summaries cannot expand approved scope. (source: request)
- Use clean fresh Build `--context FILE` for selective production reuse after protected-contract corrections, under NEW exact approval. Do not add an import framework. (source: request)
- Keep browser/Playwright/package acquisition with its separate Studio owner. No Go resumption, 014 Build, image feature, Studio tooling changes, planner/critic, automatic Intent splitting, model switch, new compaction dependency or quota/cache-benefit promise. (source: request)

### Working-window contract

Use a fixed conservative **524288 UTF-8 byte ceiling on the complete rendered outbound JSON request**, including policy/developer blocks, input, tools and request envelope, with **131072 tokens reserved for output/reasoning**. Bytes are an intentionally conservative input proxy, not observed token usage or a measured provider refusal threshold. Published Sol metadata (1050000 context, 922000 input, 128000 output) and last COMPLETED input 883138 do not establish a rejection threshold; the subsequent failed request's usage/size remain unknown. There is no new CLI/YAML setting, provider field, or total-run cap. Expose the shared calculation as `Kogen.WorkingContext.measure(body_map)`, returning `%{rendered_bytes: integer, input_budget_bytes: 524288, output_reserve_tokens: 131072, fits: boolean}` using the same serializer as transport. Equality fits; one byte above does not. Preflight must measure the request actually sent, not just conversation text.

Before every builder/reviewer request, at a completed request/tool-batch boundary, continue unchanged if it fits. If it does not fit and safe reduction exists, archive the full old window, then start an explicitly labelled new local window. Do not reset between a call and its output, during tool execution, or while execution is uncertain. Do not replay tools to manufacture completed pairs. Within an ordinary window preserve native replay items, their order, assistant phase and opaque encrypted reasoning bytes unchanged. At a reset, entire completed exchanges may move to history; opaque items are not edited, summarized or selectively spliced as if still ordinary replay. Retain the newest completed exchange intact when it fits; if an exchange itself is irreducible, stop rather than loop reset indefinitely.

Every new window carries the exact approved Intent/feature/model, README, testing rules, commands and protection, source-provenance retrieval reference and any frozen diagnostic context. It carries current candidate identity, phase and repair owner, unfinished work, unresolved findings, current honest check status and history references. Keep model-authored progress/unfinished-work/finding statements losslessly unless explicitly superseded; label them as observations, never approvals or proof. Native check results are authoritative only for their exact candidate: editing invalidates current green status; failed, unrun, stale and unknown remain distinguishable. Repeated superseded failure bodies and obsolete whole-file tool arguments may move to history. Do not infer completion from a handoff. A reviewer reset continues the same independent reviewer stage and unresolved findings, never importing the builder's reasoning or starting another whole critique.

Use a user data message starting exactly `Local working-window reset\n` followed by JSON with `version: 1`, `owner` (`build` or `review`), `phase`, `candidate_tree`, `approval_sha256`, `checks` (including `status` and candidate identity), `unfinished`, `findings`, and `history` (ordered `{path,sha256}` references). Additional native factual fields are allowed, not new authority. The runtime derives identities/status; handoff text cannot grant green/review/commit eligibility. Include a bounded progress/reset notice with measured bytes, ceiling, reserve and history reference, not raw prompts.

Archive prior windows under `.kogen/local/runs/<id>/working-context/<owner>/` as immutable ordered JSON files containing `input` arrays, linked by exact-byte SHA-256 references. Together with the checkpoint's active window these recover the full ordered replay history, including complete tool calls/outputs, exact multiline Unicode, and opaque items. Existing individual tool-output caps are unchanged; this feature introduces no further historical truncation. New custody directories are 0700 and files 0600 even under umask 022. Do not put raw history, originals, credentials or authorization headers into console or generic metadata logs. Retain old failed attempts/results/usage, not just the last window.

Checkpoint the active window, archive hashes/order, owner, phase, current findings/progress and source binding atomically with existing candidate/HEAD/index/approval/configuration guards. Resume must continue the saved owner and window without duplicating completed effects, clearing findings or laundering old evidence. Missing, changed, unsafe or unreadable referenced custody is an actionable refusal before inference or mutation. Keep no-commit-on-uncertain-tool/commit safeguards. Version-2 pre-window checkpoints may be safely supported through explicit validated migration or explicitly refused as unsupported with no changes; never silently treat absence of working state as a new Build. New checkpoints expose their continuity state in the decoded saved Build map as `working_context` and source binding as `source_provenance` (both may be nil for a genuinely absent legacy source). Unsupported legacy transitions must remain inspectable.

If mandatory material alone cannot fit, or reduction cannot make progress, fail `candidate/context_budget_exceeded` before sending the oversized request. Report role, measured/mandatory bytes, ceiling, reserve, retained checkpoint/history paths and actionable instructions to inspect custody and use ordinary Refine/new approval if scope must change. Leave candidate/index/HEAD/approval intact. Never retry the identical oversized payload, silently truncate, automatically split the Intent, or claim provider exhaustion was prevented universally. Provider context errors below the conservative proxy remain honest failures, not permission to drop authority.

### Source provenance and existing approval

On successful native Shape retain exact initial request bytes, its initial source-path label (or `-` for stdin), SHA-256, the questions/options as actually asked, exact successful answer-input bytes and resolved answers, and originating HEAD/tree/configuration identity. Success must not delete this custody with pending `state.json`. Partial/failed attempts do not replace a successful current source. Store the private current manifest at `.kogen/local/provenance/<slug>/current.json`, version 1, with `request: {text,source_path,sha256}`, `rounds` in order, `corrections` in order, `contract_sha256` (the normal complete protected baseline hash) and `comparison`. Preserve immutable prior manifests when successfully refining. Each round includes original `input` and the actual `questions` and settled `answers`; a correction includes its exact text/path/hash and prior contract identity. No automatic Git addition/commit of originals. These are not credentials stores.

Have the existing shaper compare requested behaviors and settled non-secret literals against its actual complete proposed contract, with bounded `## Source comparison` prose in the Intent, and a manifest comparison copied from that report, not a claimed mechanical semantic proof. Use statuses addressed, omitted, conflicting, superseded with source/contract references. Do not expose secrets or raw private originals in that public report. Approval cards show the private manifest path/hash, current contract binding, bounded comparison and retrieval instructions, including omitted/conflicting literals. Approval still requires the normal explicit current hash; there is no new critic/review/approval stage. A mapping is an aid, never proof of semantic completeness. A deliberate scope change is recorded as such; latest settled answers/corrections remain distinguishable from obsolete originals.

Bind the approved manifest identity in the approval/run custody without making private raw bytes tracked baseline files. Build and fresh independent review receive a labelled diagnostic provenance reference with retrieval instructions and the rule that only approved Intent is implementation authority. Provide exact full originals through ordinary native read tools, not mandatory repeated giant prompt injection. An omission such as a missing HTML title suffix or wrong personal-repository example must be surfaced at shaping/card comparison; fixing missing scope requires ordinary native Refine/new exact approval, not an original-request override. Freeze the successful bound source for Build/resume even if the caller's input files change or vanish. Existing projects with no source receipt remain usable and are explicitly labelled `Source provenance: unavailable (legacy)`; never reconstruct originals from Intent prose. Corrupt or changed bound receipts are not equivalent to legacy absence and must refuse before inference/mutation.

Successful native Refine retains the original source and appends its exact correction and previous contract identity, updates the report/binding, archives the prior source manifest and revokes the old approval by the existing rules. Failed/refused Refine leaves the successful source and approval unchanged. Changed source/comparison never silently inherits exact approval. Native pending continuation consumes only actual numbered answers; the complete request/context is not interpreted as inferred answers.

### Existing reuse and delivery boundaries

After a protected-contract correction, preserve native production work and a hash manifest externally, obtain fresh approval, then start production-clean with `kogen intent build <slug> --context FILE`. That diagnostic handoff names absolute archived native production paths/hashes and useful obsolete findings. The native builder may inspect and selectively reproduce suitable production contents. No automatic stash/patch/tree replay, old protected bytes, approval/check-state import, or old green results. Verify and independently review the new candidate normally. Resume accepts no new context. Maintain README/usage and the affected maintained prose/Gherkin/Quint specifications; run their distinct `cd spec && sh check.sh` wrapper as well as configured gates. Do not edit `.formatter.exs`, `mix.exs` or `.kogen/project.yaml` for this delivery.

The supplied source baseline is signed/pushed 10ce2eaf7ccf9dbb84efeb26a30fec19d4a7b717, tree bf2bfb03f3408ab574247d05056070dffd902a2e. Root adoption has passed; pending-status history is not a hold. Freeze the qualified private driver `/Users/almirsarajcic/Areas/Kogen/studio-work/kogen-repairs/shaping-evidence-quality-20261021/delivery/installed-10ce2eaf`; do not overwrite any active prefix. Standing overnight delegation permits ordinary native exact delegated approval/Build/qualification/sign/push after actual inspection, not a fabricated human hash approval. This Intent does not implement installation/adoption automation. Keep Cache042 OPEN; unchanged transport needs no new account/API probe.

## Tests
- Rendered-next-request conservative calculation and adjacent boundary: shared measure function, complete JSON and multiline Unicode cases (unit)
- Local resets bound actual builder and reviewer traffic while retaining authority, ordered completed exchanges, opaque/phase bytes and honest progress: installed fake-provider growth journeys with independent archive/wire observations (scenario)
- Irreducible mandatory inputs stop before provider/effects with actionable custody: oversized approved README journey (regression)
- Private archive integrity and saved-owner interruption/resume retain effects/findings and exact safety guards: installed completed-boundary stop/resume and changed-archive refusal (integration)
- Check statuses never become green for edited candidates and reset cannot clear reviewer blockers: focused status transitions plus existing blocked-review/final-verification tests extended across resets (integration)
- Durable request/Q&A source identity, comparison, retrieval and non-authority at approval/Build/fresh review: installed Shape questions, exact answers and literal-omission card journey (scenario)
- Successful Refine updates source lineage and requires fresh approval while failed Refine preserves prior source: installed native correction success/refusal journeys (integration)
- Legacy source absence remains usable and pre-window checkpoints are migrated safely or honestly refused: real decoded saved checkpoint transition and legacy fixture journey (integration)
- Bound source corruption cannot masquerade as absence or change a resumed request: changed/deleted input and changed bound receipt cases (integration)
- Protected-correction selective production reuse uses only existing clean fresh --context and fresh gates: installed context handoff with absolute archive path/hash, protected injection counterexample and no automatic import (scenario)
- Existing verification, review independence, uncertain effects, exact approval and commit eligibility are unchanged: affected existing installed integration/scenario tests and maintained spec wrapper (existing)

## Feasibility
- Local windows use unchanged stateless transport; no provider capability obligation is introduced. The model typechecked and Safety passed seed 21, 100 samples, 40 steps on Quint TypeScript. (probe 1: exit 0, 0.5 s)
- After the first readiness observation exposed unspaced Elixir `!=` comparisons, a focused scratch compile of the corrected fixture succeeded; it did not execute acceptance or establish product support. Subsequent native readiness reached actual missing-feature assertions. (probe 2: exit 0, 1.2 s)

# Keep dependency edits compatible with checks

Slug: usable-check-protection
Model: .kogen/intents/usable-check-protection/model.qnt invariants=ConflictIsNotReady,ProtectedChangeNeverLands,LandedWasApproved seed=19 samples=100 steps=12
Acceptance:
- .kogen/intents/usable-check-protection/acceptance.feature
- features/steps/usable_check_protection_steps.js

Repair KOGEN-001 and KOGEN-006 at init and shaping, not by changing Studio or weakening Build. Today Init.validate/2 checks only that proposed protect paths are tracked; Init.merge/2 unions them with detection. Shape.context/5 supplies commands but not protect, and submit has no conflict outcome. Replace that selection contract and incomplete shaping context with the rules below. Existing manually committed project configuration remains authoritative; do not migrate, silently rewrite, or unprotect it. In particular this repair does not need to edit this checkout's protected mix.exs or .kogen/project.yaml.

Init protection means verification definitions/settings, not every input read by a check. A dependency manifest or lockfile is not eligible merely because it declares dependencies or is consumed by formatting, compilation, tests, vet, audit, or setup. Enforce this at the real init proposal boundary, before writing configuration: reject an ineligible protect entry with a path-specific explanation, use the existing single correction request, and retain the existing provider/init_invalid exit 4/no-writes behavior if the second proposal is invalid. Do not silently accept or silently delete the bad entry. Valid corrected proposals merge as before; detected formatter/linter configuration and passing commands must survive.

Use a small content/role rule, not language discovery: distinguish dependency metadata from actual verification definitions in the manifest formats already at issue (Mix project, npm package, nested Go module and their lockfiles). mix.exs with ordinary project/dependency metadata and cli/go.mod are editable inputs. A combined manifest with executable check definitions or embedded check settings is not dependency-only: for example package.json containing the scripts used by npm checks, or a Mix project defining the executable check alias used by a configured command, can legitimately remain whole-file protected. Dedicated formatter/linter/suppression settings remain eligible. No arbitrary evaluation of Mix code, broad file classifier, new Go detection, field-level baseline, or manifest-name blanket exemption is required. Keep actual checks unchanged when a manifest remains editable; the builder/reviewer must not weaken verification through its editable portions. Whole-file protection remains whole-file protection: an explicitly protected combined manifest cannot receive a dependency-only exception during Build.

Supply shaping with the configured protect patterns, their currently matched paths (using the existing public protection expansion), and the automatic baseline contract (Intent files, Acceptance paths and .kogen/project.yaml). State explicitly that approval freezes that baseline, not an exception to it. Extend the shaper's submit tool with an exclusive blocked result: `{"blocked":{"paths":["relative/protected/path"],"reason":"why the requested change requires this edit"}}`. This is a report, never an authorization. Validate nonempty paths/reason and that each path is actually protected under the current contract; reuse current protection semantics, including globs. Do not infer required edits by scanning arbitrary request prose. Teach the shaper to inspect required edits and use blocked when a required protected edit cannot be avoided without changing the requested outcome. It must not submit a ready package conditional on an unavailable protected-edit approval mechanism. Blocked writes no new Intent/approval and starts no Build; files from an earlier not-ready attempt retain the existing SHP-4 semantics. End with exit 1, `shape/protected_conflict: required edits touch protected files: <paths>` in submitted order, the supplied reason, and `Next: revise the request, or review and commit .kogen/project.yaml outside Build, then shape again; preserve checks and actual check configuration. There is no protected-edit override.` The supported manual configuration review is outside Build, changes the approval baseline, and must not be portrayed as approval of a protected edit. Do not add a new bypass, builder tool, flag, or general readiness/prose analyzer. If the caller retains legitimate whole-file protection, revising the request is the available path.

Align SET-8/SET-11, SHP-3/4/7/8 and VER-1/8 prose and affected scenarios/catalog with executable behavior. Update docs/configuration.md and README guidance on editable dependency manifests versus immutable verification configuration and on genuine conflicts. Update README/development guidance so installed self-hosting is a qualification path: attempt the documented Studio/Kogen loop first; an unavailable required self-hosting path permits an external-engine repair, preserving original evidence and independently verifying the result. It is not an absolute ban on external repairs. Keep ordinary local signing/identity behavior, no push/publication and no AI-attribution trailers.

Evidence discipline: the observed init artifact had exactly [.formatter.exs, mix.exs, cli/go.mod]; source and generated artifacts demonstrate the conflict. Studio Build a22a312e was interrupted before verification/review/commit, not a failed Build reproduction. Build d8dacd7f was also interrupted before implementation edits/verification/review/commit. Do not mutate the supplied outside evidence, Studio checkout, issue register, or implementation remnants. The driving caller will install the fixed committed release and retry Studio from its generated baseline without hand-editing generated config/specs. The deterministic regression here uses a local path dependency rather than external Ecto downloads; it qualifies the same manifest/protection contract, not the final Studio runtime feature.

This replacement corrects the independent harness, not the product scope. The existing dispatcher takes the regex source `^the caller is signed in to ChatGPT$`, without slash delimiters. Use that API unchanged. The qualification prepares a warning-free temporary ex-app source because the existing detection fixture deliberately contains a compile warning; the regression requires all seven checks to pass. Only the external provider responses are scripted; files, Git, installed engine, initialization, approval, Build protection, checks and review wiring remain real. Command output is retained in the receipt for useful failure details. The four acceptance cases and Quint model are unchanged. Build implements the production repair; do not change helper APIs to accommodate the old invalid caller or add a second backend. The harness uses KOGEN_ARCHIVE when supplied, otherwise the existing suite's newest-release selection; qualification of the repaired implementation requires its freshly packaged archive.

## Decisions
- Preserve checks and dedicated formatter/linter/suppression protection while dependency-only manifests evolve for approved features; reject the observed bad protection proposal instead of silently freezing manifests. (source: request)
- Keep combined verification manifests whole-file protected where they really define checks; no selective protected-edit bypass is introduced. (source: request)
- Report genuine protection conflicts before presenting an Intent as build-ready, naming the actual supported next action without changing configuration. (source: request)
- Try installed self-hosting first, allow external-engine repair when a required path fails, preserve evidence, verify independently, and permit ordinary local signed commits without push or AI-attribution trailers. (source: request)
- Correct the generated harness against the frozen installed fd0cdcfb archive, preserve the four cases/model and formatter protection assertions, and leave production implementation to Build. (source: request)

## Tests
- Init rejects dependency-only protection but accepts real verification definitions, preserving its one-correction/no-writes contract: extend the focused public Init.validate tests in test/kogen/detect_test.exs for ordinary Mix/Go/lock metadata versus npm check scripts, Mix check aliases and dedicated settings, and retain existing invalid-twice coverage (unit)
- The observed bad init proposal must not freeze ordinary dependency edits or remove the seven passing checks and formatter protection: the independent installed-release acceptance scenario initializes from the exact bad protect list, receives correction feedback, shapes, approves and lands both manifest edits without editing generated config/specs (regression)
- Formatter/check configuration stays immutable during Build even when dependency inputs are editable: the acceptance formatter scenario uses a shell mutation and verifies baseline_changed, no commit and unchanged configuration; retain existing write_file refusal tests unchanged (regression)
- A combined manifest defining actual checks is not blanket-unprotected and a manually configured manifest protection is respected: the acceptance conflict outline covers both npm check scripts and manually committed mix.exs protection, asserting no ready package, no approval/Build and unchanged configuration (regression)
- Shaping receives the effective protection contract and can honestly report a required protected edit: the acceptance conflict outline asserts the provider-visible context/tool schema and the real blocked submission output; add focused invalid blocked-submission cases alongside the existing SHP-4 integration tests, without duplicating the successful conflict flow (integration)
- Existing setup, approval hashing, baseline mutation guards, verification, review and ordinary commit signing remain in force: retain the existing setup/approval/build/verification/commit suites and update only changed spec scenarios and step catalog clauses (existing)

## Feasibility
- Located the frozen fd0cdcfb archive in dist/ and the preserved first harness outside the checkout; the locating command's final optional directory listing was absent. No original evidence was changed. (probe 1: exit 1, 1.5 s)

The receipt showed initCode=0 and initCalls=1 instead of 2, with the exact bad protection list; it also exposed the ex-app fixture's intentional compile warning, which caused init to omit compile. (probe 2: exit 1, 21.7 s)
- With warning-free temporary fixture source and command diagnostics, all seven checks survived init. The dependency run reached candidate/baseline_changed for mix.exs; the formatter run reached candidate/baseline_changed for .formatter.exs with unchanged HEAD/configuration; both conflict modes reached the old shaper's shape/invalid_output response because blocked is unsupported. These were inspected behavioral failures, not setup exceptions or timeouts. (probe 3: exit 1, 62.2 s)
- An auxiliary run varied only the external provider's init proposal to the valid [.formatter.exs] list, without editing generated configuration/specifications or production code. The installed frozen engine shaped, approved, built, passed acceptance and all seven checks, obtained review approval and landed both manifest edits with formatter/configuration unchanged. This separately qualified the downstream fake-provider/tool/CLI wiring; the submitted regression still starts with the exact observed invalid proposal. (probe 4: exit 0, 19.4 s)
- The exact replacement harness and unchanged four-case feature ran against the frozen installed fd0cdcfb archive. All four When steps completed; all four Then steps failed on missing product behavior, and the message report recorded exactly four test cases. Dependency/formatter cases failed at initCalls=1 versus 2; manual-mix retained the old unusable protect list; npm-scripts lacked protection context and the blocked tool, with shape/invalid_output rather than the required conflict output.
